01_fare_distribution.png: Fares are right-skewed: most trips cluster around ₹100-250, with a long tail of expensive long/airport trips up to ~₹1020.
02_distance_vs_fare.png: Fare rises roughly linearly with distance (strong positive trend); the regression line confirms distance is the dominant price driver.
03_top_pickup_fare.png: Airport/border/pilgrimage endpoints command the highest average fares, confirming special-zone flags add predictive value.
03_top_dropoff_fare.png: Airport/border/pilgrimage endpoints command the highest average fares, confirming special-zone flags add predictive value.
04_fare_boxplot_top_locations.png: Fare spread widens for high-value locations (airport/border), while inner-city trips stay tightly clustered at lower fares.
05_fare_by_hour.png: Fares peak in the morning (8-9) and evening (17-19) rush windows and dip at night, matching the rush_hour flag.
06_fare_by_dow.png: Weekend days (5,6) show slightly higher average fares than weekdays.
07_weekend_vs_weekday.png: Weekend trips are modestly more expensive on average than weekday trips.
08_rush_hour_vs_normal.png: Rush-hour trips carry a small fare premium over normal-hour trips.
09_night_vs_day.png: Night trips (22:00-06:00) are slightly pricier, consistent with a night surcharge in the data.
10_flag_effect_on_fare.png: Airport and border trips have the highest average fares; market and pilgrimage trips also cost more than ordinary trips.
11_correlation_heatmap.png: distance_km correlates most strongly with fare_amount; special-zone flags (especially airport/border) show moderate positive correlation.
12_fare_heatmap_pickup_dropoff.png: Airport/border pairs (e.g. Wagah Border <-> Amritsar Airport) sit at the top of the fare matrix, confirming long cross-city trips cost most.
